scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

  ip link set eth1 down

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Both fabric-facing uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 — eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, spine_router_0_0 side) and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, spine_router_0_1 side) — are administratively DOWN. The host-facing interface eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) remains UP.

**Mechanism:** With eth0 and eth1 down, leaf_router_0_1 cannot complete any TCP handshake with its BGP peers. BGP's state machine therefore stays in the `Active` state (repeatedly attempting to open a connection) for both spine sessions. Without established BGP sessions, leaf_router_0_1 receives no eBGP routes and advertises no routes upstream. Its kernel RIB contains only the directly-connected 10.0.1.0/24 prefix. Any packet destined outside that subnet is dropped, and the router generates ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" — exactly the message pc_0_1 receives when trying to reach 10.0.0.2.

**Localization:** leaf_router_0_1, interfaces eth0 and eth1 (both show `state DOWN`, no LOWER_UP flag, while the peer ends at spine_router_0_0:eth2 and spine_router_0_1:eth2 remain UP).

**Root cause:** Both uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 were taken down (link_down fault), severing all spine connectivity and collapsing both eBGP sessions, leaving pc_0_1 isolated from the rest of the fabric.

**Fix:** Restore the interfaces with `ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1; BGP sessions will re-establish, routes will be exchanged, and pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1 reachability will recover.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names leaf_router_0_1 as the localized device with both fabric-facing uplinks down.
